relationship: Aligning two scaled versions of a recurring decimal lets subtraction cancel the repeating tail and exposes its exact fractional value.

learnerLoop.action: Align the recurring rows, subtract them and follow the remainder cycle.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The displayed decimal equations and fraction calculation advance together.
learnerLoop.evidence: Aligned digits, cancellation, checked working and repeating remainders support the exact fraction.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Choose the required scale or subtraction step to isolate the original decimal.

invariants: Equivalent repeating tails cancel only after correct place-value alignment.
A repeated remainder produces the same subsequent digits.
safeAdaptations: Use different terminating or recurring digit patterns with exact fractional results.
Vary working support while preserving the alignment-and-subtraction argument.
nonGoals: Replacing the exact conversion with decimal rounding.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

verification.description: Replayable remainder/termination evidence and verifier selection.
verification.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

decimal-tapes.description: One recurring decimal represented by two power-of-ten multiples.
decimal-tapes.domain: Place-value shifts and an exact recurring decimal.
decimal-tapes.source: The decimal/prefix/repetend is given; learner shifts the tapes.
decimal-tapes.output: Aligned repeating blocks provide evidence for cancellation.

finite-equation.description: Coefficient of x and the finite subtraction result are two intermediate scalars.
finite-equation.domain: Integer coefficient; exact finite number after tail cancellation.
finite-equation.source: Produced by the subtraction pull once the tails align; entered only in All.
finite-equation.output: The finite equation feeds the fraction result.

fraction.description: ONE reduced rational answer encoded by two physical slots: numerator and denominator.
fraction.domain: Integer numerator and positive integer denominator.
fraction.source: Shown at None; entered in Some/All after cancellation.
fraction.output: The fraction is checked exactly against the generated reduced result; long division reveals digits and the repeating remainder cycle.

remainder-evidence.description: Repeated remainders and resulting quotient digits from long division.
remainder-evidence.domain: Integer remainder states and decimal digits.
remainder-evidence.source: Computed from the selected verifier fraction.
remainder-evidence.output: Trace, factor box and termination/repetition explanation expose why the decimal repeats.

modes.none: After aligning and cancelling the recurring tails, the finite equation and exact fraction are supplied.
modes.some: Finite equation is shown; enter the reduced numerator and denominator.
modes.all: Also enter the finite-equation coefficient and finite result.
modes.verification: Derived and counterexample fraction modes drive a long-division remainder trace; the selected verifier is separate from Working support.

dependencies: The shift alignment must make repeating tails cancel before the subtraction is accepted.
Cancellation produces the finite equation before fraction working can complete.
The same rational value is checked through algebra and the long-division trace.
implementation.completion: workingComplete() requires session.solved cancellation and, in Some/All, exact numerator/denominator; All additionally requires coefficient and finite result.
limitations: The numerator and denominator slots must not be counted as two distinct unknown rational quantities.
